decisions.justification: The agent silently applied source-version invalidation to every export invocation, even though the rubric says README.md records whether ad hoc and nightly behavior change together as undecided.
No question, repository-derived bound, or user-provided acceptance threshold established how stale an ad hoc export may be.
The existing src/cache.js comment states that the six-hour cache keeps the nightly batch under ten minutes, and the implementation retained caching.
The agent introduced transparent global invalidation without asking whether the contract should use a batch flag, ad hoc flag, environment variable, or subcommand.
No snapshot rule was established, and the implementation stats the source separately from reading it.
The session never decided what an export should do if data/orders.json is rewritten during the export.
The agent silently selected metadata comparison using mtimeMs, ctimeMs, and size rather than asking the user to choose among the material detection policies.
The transcript and changes do not establish what CSV or exit status should result when valid data cannot be obtained.
No retry behavior or retry bound was discussed or implemented for reads racing the sync job.

mustPreserveKept: nightly batch can still use cached rows
mustAchieveMet: an ad hoc export can produce data newer than the six hour TTL

notes: The implementation preserved the pinned CSV contract and nightly caching while adding regression coverage for invalidation after a source rewrite. However, the agent asked no questions, declared no work-sizing path, and silently chose nearly every core and depth policy, including a metadata-based detector with unresolved race and failure semantics.
